answer: Karst dye-tracer proof — one $27 bottle of crystal violet tracer dye per identity, poured into the sinkhole feeding one named karst spring. The spring's downstream monitor logs the dye's arrival curve; the auditor matches it against that spring's published transit time, and a forged curve misses the peak by hours and fails. A second identity claiming the same spring repeats the same curve, so the pair is struck. Dye flows one way through basalt-capped conduits no farm can reroute, and a tracer poured from a desk reaches no spring at all.
